newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.05 up at 41.25 to the dollar in the kerb market on Tuesday amid higher dollar supplies from abroad, dealers said.
The rupee was likely to open stable on Wednesday, one dealer of Khanani and Kalia said.
The State (central) bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on April 23, was 40.2400/40.4412 to the dollar.
The premium on the foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 2.70 percent compared to the opening at 2.60 percent.
